lines.en: label day270:
scene norikomayaoffice1
: Hah...
I lean back in my chair and try to figure out what is happening to my life.
And when I say “my” life I mean “Sensei’s” life because, as I was reminded via brute force yesterday, it is very much not my own.
It’s one thing to have some girl randomly show up and talk about how she’s apparently known me for her entire life-
But it’s another thing to proclaim her love for me in front of a room full of girls sliding down a slippery slope toward that same end point.
The biggest surprise wasn’t that at all, though.
It was how Maya (Of all people) reacted to the whole thing.
She didn’t even show up to[school] today.
And sure, it’s not the first time that’s happened...
But to just chalk an absence up to coincidence after that outburst would be dismissing something anyone with half a brain would know is peculiar.
According to Ami, she didn’t even get back to the dorm until late last night.
But is Noriko knowing me from the past really cause for such an uncharacteristic explosion?
: Sensei~ This is your office, right?
: It’s me! Noriko!
: The girl with the pink hair who asked you to wait outside the classroom only to have you march all the way down here without saying anything.
: You can come in, Noriko.
scene norikomayaoffice2
: Why, thank you for inviting me.
: No problem. Sorry I didn’t wait for you. My mind’s been a little preoccupied over the last 24 hours.
: I bet. Probably weird having me show up again out of nowhere and then saying all that stuff about being in love with you.
: A little bit, yeah.
scene norikomayaoffice3
: Well, it was weird for me too! I don’t think I’ve ever cried in front of so many people before.
: In fact, I can’t even remember the last time I cried in general.
: I’ve been saving all of my tears for the moment we reunited and they just kinda came streaming out all at once.
: I’m kind of excited to never have to cry again, though.
: You are most definitely going to cry again at some point.
scene norikomayaoffice4
: Nope. No time for crying. Gotta make you remember me any way I possibly can.
: Even if it means dressing up in clothes that are way too small for me and reenacting all of the time we used to spend together.
: I think the clothes you’re wearing now are perfectly fine.
: Okaaaay~ But if you ever change your mind, just let me know.
: Pretty sure I could act it out quite nicely since every second I’ve ever spent with you has been playing on repeat in my head since the moment we separated.
: It’s how I’ve kept myself sane all these years.
: Well, mostly sane.
: Pretty sane.
: I don’t know. Lots of people at my old[school] called me crazy because I would bring a pocket knife to[school], but it’s not like I ever stabbed someone, you know?
: Do you...have a pocket knife with you now?
scene norikomayaoffice5
: Just this little one for self defense. You never know when someone is going to pull you into an alleyway and tear your skirt off, you know?
scene norikomayaoffice6
: You can pull me into any alleyway you want, though.
: In fact, I encourage it.
: Are you even allowed to carry that with you?
: I don’t know. Does it make you uncomfortable?
: Yes. Please put it away.
scene norikomayaoffice4
: Done.
: There you go. Proof I’m not crazy.
: I’m...probably going to need a little more proof than that.
: No offense, but everything you’ve done since coming here has been a little bit over the top.
scene norikomayaoffice7
: Hey, wait a second!
: I’m not the one who freaked out and called someone a cunt in the middle of class.
: If there’s anyone who’s crazy, it’s Maya. Not me.
: I wouldn’t be surprised if she carried some sort of weapon with her too.
: Just...keep the knife in your pocket and everything will be fine.
scene norikomayaoffice8
: Oh, I don’t have any pockets. And I don’t carry a purse either. So I kind of keep it tucked into the side of my underwear.
: This one time, it slipped out and totally sliced my leg wide open and all of the blood made people think I was on my period.
: I’m fine now, though. And I heal quickly so there's not even a scar anymore.
: Awesome, right?
scene norikomayaoffice9
: Oh my god I missed you so fucking much.
: I still can’t believe I’m seeing you again.
: It’s like...a dream come true.
: I can tell...
: I just wish I knew a little more about...well, what our relationship was.
scene norikomayaoffice10
: I’m actually your girlfriend.
: We have a house in Okinomiya and should get moving right away since I forgot to feed our cat this morning.
: Uh-huh. And what was our actual relationship?
scene norikomayaoffice11
: We were neighbors for a really long time.
: Back when you lived in the old district.
scene yumis5
scene norikomayaoffice11
: You used to come over all the time. My parents really liked you, too.
: You were like another member of the family.
scene norikomayaoffice12
: What’s with that look?
: You know I was telling the truth that time, right?
: It seems that way, but...
: But what?
: I’m just trying to figure out why I would visit a girl your age.
: There has to be a good fifteen years between us.
: Hmm...
scene norikomayaoffice13
: Well you were at that age...
: And we can’t help who we’re into, sooooo...
scene norikomayaoffice14
: You were never there for me.
: You came over to hang out with my sister.
: Please tell me she is an older sister.
: Of course she’s an older sister...
scene norikomayaoffice15
: But...after that...thing happened, you just stopped coming over.
: Which no one ever blamed you for. It must have been really hard.
Thing?
She’s talking about the accident, right?
The one that forced Ami’s parents out of this world long before they were meant to leave.
I’ve known this girl for that long?
: So, you haven’t seen me since that accident?
scene norikomayaoffice16
: Hm?
: No, I saw you plenty of times after that. That was just the first time you disappeared.
: I’m not sure how far back your memory goes, but you used to be a tutor.
: And my parents knew how much I liked you, so the second they heard about it from Nee-chan they called you and...voila.
: Unrequited love began to blossom.
scene norikomayaoffice17
: To be honest, I kind of hate myself for never even considering that you might have gone off and become a real teacher.
: If I had known that, finding you would have been a million times easier.
: Like, I know it’s only been a few years since then, but...
: I can’t help like feel it's been way...way longer.
: Almost like I’ve been searching for you for an eternity.
scene norikomayaoffice18
: But I guess that’s just how everything feels when you love someone who doesn’t love you back, huh?
Noriko remains quiet and stares at me for several seconds. Or maybe it’s minutes.
I don’t know.
It’s kind of shocking how much this girl knows about “me.”
I don’t even think I’ve heard this much detail from Ami, and now I’m getting all of it just hoisted onto me out of nowhere.
: Sensei...Even with how long it’s been, my feelings never changed.
: You stole my heart all those years ago and now I have to steal yours. It’s only fair.
: Good luck. I don’t think there’s very much left of it.
scene norikomayaoffice19
: Ha! Now you’re starting to sound the same way you did back when you tutored me.
: But, I guess that’s also kind of depressing given the circumstances of why you began to speak like that in the first place, so forget I laughed.
: I’m just nervous. That’s all.
A knock on the door interrupts the conversation and-
scene norikomayaoffice20
And Maya suddenly walks in.
: Why knock if you’re just going to let yourself in?
: Shut up.
: Noriko, go home.
: But I don’t know which dorm I’m staying in yet.
: Then sleep in an Internet cafe or something.
: I need to talk to Sensei.
: Hmmm...
: How about we talk to him together? For old time’s sake?
scene norikomayaoffice21
: I’d rather drink bleach.
: You had your turn for “office hours” and now it’s mine.
: Now get lost or I’ll tell the principal you’re already infringing on[school] policy and have you expelled.
scene norikomayaoffice22
: You’re...threatening to tell on me?...
: How old are you?
: Hah...Fine...Fine.
: I have a shift soon anyway, so I have to get going.
scene norikomayaoffice23
: See you in class tomorrow, Sensei~
: Don’t have too much fun alone with Maya, okay?
: I rarely do.
: See you tomorrow, Noriko.
scene norikomayaoffice24
scene norikomayaoffice25
: You changed clothes.
: I changed clothes.
: Mind if I ask why?
: I don’t know, character development?
: What do you want me to say?
: Nothing really. You look cute.
: I know.
: You should stop coming to[school] for the next two months or so.
: Wait, what? I’d lose my job.
: You’d get it back once the world resets. Consider it a vacation.
: It’s not a vacation if I can’t see you, Maya.
scene norikomayaoffice26
: Stop messing around! I’m being serious!
: You’re always being serious. What’s so bad about Noriko?
: I’m not going to just blindly do what you tell me if you’re not willing to explain yourself.
: I don’t know how to explain myself, though! She’s not supposed to be here, so I never considered having to explain myself!
: How is her appearance in the[school] any worse than Uta’s or Io’s? Or any of the other transfer students?
: What’s so dangerous about me learning more about the old Sensei’s backstory when I’m so clearly not him?
scene norikomayaoffice27
scene norikomayaoffice28
: I don’t like her.
: Yeah, you’ve made that extremely clear.
: I didn’t realize there was anyone capable of getting that sort of reaction out of you.
: Yeah, well...I didn’t realize the past was something I would ever have to confront.
: Spending so much time inside of loops clearly has some adverse side effects.
: Let’s say for argument’s sake that you are not the “old” Sensei-
: I thought that was pretty much confirmed?
: Let’s say for argument’s sake that you are not the “old” Sensei- and your past was reintroduced to you by someone who just so happens to claim to know some aspects of it.
: In what way would that person’s words influence the decisions you make in your new, unrelated life?
: They wouldn’t, really.
: Then what can you possibly gain from hearing them?
: The best course of action for you is to continue what you’re doing now- not looking too deeply into things and just...existing the way any other selfish, morally-inept person exists.
: You made it to winter. Do you have any idea how many “you’s” have made it to winter?
: Am I allowed to find out or is that also part of your “stop looking into the past” thing?
scene norikomayaoffice29
: When do I ever ask you for anything?
: You ask me to leave you alone pretty much every time I see you.
: That doesn’t count. That’s how things are supposed to be.
: When have I ever asked you to do something that I, Maya Makinami, am not personally at the forefront of?
: I’m trying to preserve your life.
: Noriko can ruin everything much quicker than you think she can.
: Huh...
: ...What?
: I’m just trying to figure out how you would know that if it’s something you never dealt with before.
: See?
: You don’t know for sure, do you?
: You’re just scared because the world isn’t something you understand anymore.
scene norikomayaoffice30
: You’re right.
: I abhor the idea of admitting it, but you’re right.
: Your sudden tendency to weave through failure unscathed is becoming more of a burden than it has been in a very long time.
: I’m very scared.
: But I’d be a lot less scared if you ceased communications with Noriko.
: There. You got me to admit something.
: Now you know how serious I am about this.
: Please.
I sigh to myself and get out of my chair.
Never have I felt so far away, yet so close to someone at the same time.
It’s kind of like Maya is trying to prevent me from falling off a cliff by tying a blindfold around my eyes.
It’s not a solution, but it makes everything a lot less miserable and more...mysterious, I guess.
But, inside of this makeshift metaphor, we don’t even know the cliff is a cliff yet.
It could be a diving board into a giant pool of money and pillows. And cake.
It could be something wonderful.
I am a man who understands the sheer harm that simply knowing something can cause.
But I am also a man who would willingly discard that knowledge as I am one who thinks with his penis just as much as his mind.
More than his mind, even.
Noriko might be dangerous, and she might wind up revealing something that hurts Maya.
But how often does Maya actually get hurt?
She’s blowing this out of proportion.
She has to be.
That’s all this is.
: Maya-
scene norikomayaoffice31
: You don’t have to say anything...I can tell how you feel from your expression alone.
: You’re going to do what you want and don’t care one way or the other what implications it may have for the future.
: If it’s any consolation, you’re still my favorite shrine maiden.
: Sometimes, forcing people to do things they’re not comfortable with is the best way to move them forward.
: My own philosophies spell my downfall once again.
: It’s not a downfall, it’s-
: It’s a spiral.
: I’m going home now.
scene black
I watch as Maya leaves the room.
When she reaches for the handle, it’s the closest I’ve ever seen her hands to shaking.
I’m sure she’ll be fine.
